taxonomic_note: Canonical genus corrected from source-pool Panicum obtusum to current Hopia obtusa. Panicum obtusum remains an important field-guide synonym.
look_here_first: FIRST trace the long aboveground vine-like stolon to a SWOLLEN, hairy node with actual roots and young shoot (if visible) on the same live plant. THEN verify the contracted narrow seedhead of rounded, blunt spikelets. The four new Harms source photographs show reproductive branches, stem and collar but NOT one verified connected root-to-seed voucher. Compare Cynodon terminal fingers; do not call a node 'rooted' from a merely hairy stem macro.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Kew/POWO accepts Hopia obtusa and lists Texas in its native range; Panicum obtusum is a homotypic synonym. The project Hays County native source pool records the taxon under Panicum obtusum. The Balcones Canyonlands Preserve plant list explicitly records vine mesquite (Panicum obtusum) in Travis County. The Texas Hill Country grass treatment documents Hopia obtusa as a widespread Hill Country species; Blanco County is retained from the project's reviewed Hill Country source set.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: Occurrence is not treated as nativity; introduced records do not count toward the three-county native threshold.

best_field_traits: WARM SEASON: native perennial forming patches/sod, sometimes found where runoff lingers; season and habitat are supporting clues only.
STOLONS: long slender tough aboveground runners can connect shoots; they are not simply loose roots.
ROOTING NODES: prominent swollen, often densely hairy/villous joints along stolons may root and produce new growth; photograph same connected runner.
SEEDHEAD: narrow upright panicle of 1–4 relatively short appressed raceme-like branches along central axis; may look like a single short spike from afar.
SPIKELETS: fairly large for this fine grass, blunt rounded oval, approximately 3–4 mm, generally smooth and without protruding awns; confirm with a scale and lens.
LEAVES: relatively flat to rolled blue-green blades, often 2–7 mm wide; size and glaucous color overlap with other grasses.
LIGULE: an actual membrane about 1–2 mm, not a fringe of hairs; do not infer it from fuzzy stolon nodes.
morphology_keys.joey_family_training: Poaceae family training: identify inflorescence architecture first, then inspect spikelets/glumes/lemma-palea/awns and ligule-collar-sheath characters.

comparisons.key_distinctions: BERMUDAGRASS (Cynodon dactylon) also creeps by stolons but usually has 3–7 slender DIGITATE one-sided fingers radiating near one point, rather than Hopia's narrow head of short appressed branches with stout blunt OVAL spikelets; its ligule is a short hair-fringed membranous rim. SWITCHGRASS (Panicum virgatum) normally forms taller erect clumps from rhizomes with a large open much-branched panicle, not vine mesquite's long aboveground node-rooting stolons. BUFFALOGRASS (Bouteloua dactyloides) is low sod-forming and dioecious, with contrasting separate male/female flowering structures rather than vine mesquite's oval spikelets. Do not identify from a vegetative patch or seedhead shape alone; trace the node and examine attached spikelets.

field_id_finish_pass.crew_teaching_summary: VINE MESQUITE: FIRST trace a long creeping aboveground STOLON away from a leafy shoot; examine a swollen, densely hairy node where a new plant can root. THEN look at the narrow upright seedhead: short appressed raceme-like branches carry conspicuous smooth, rounded/oval blunt spikelets (not bermudagrass's radiating fingers). A tiny membranous ligule at the blade/sheath junction confirms a grass collar character but is not identified from the current photographs. Spikelets and root-bearing nodes must belong to the same plant.
field_id_finish_pass.lookalikes: BERMUDAGRASS (Cynodon dactylon) also creeps by stolons but usually has 3–7 slender DIGITATE one-sided fingers radiating near one point, rather than Hopia's narrow head of short appressed branches with stout blunt OVAL spikelets; its ligule is a short hair-fringed membranous rim. SWITCHGRASS (Panicum virgatum) normally forms taller erect clumps from rhizomes with a large open much-branched panicle, not vine mesquite's long aboveground node-rooting stolons. BUFFALOGRASS (Bouteloua dactyloides) is low sod-forming and dioecious, with contrasting separate male/female flowering structures rather than vine mesquite's oval spikelets. Do not identify from a vegetative patch or seedhead shape alone; trace the node and examine attached spikelets.
critical_photo_gaps: Same rooted Hopia plant photographed wide enough to trace one long aboveground stolon to a new rooted shoot; include a metric scale.
10–20× macro of an ACTUAL swollen hairy stolon node visibly emitting adventitious roots; do not arrow a nonrooting joint.
1-mm-scale inner MEMBRANOUS ligule at the leaf blade/sheath junction, with collar hairs separately visible if present.
10–20× side and face views of an intact attached ~3–4 mm rounded blunt spikelet showing glumes/veins; avoid claiming venation from distant seedheads.
Matched same-scale comparison: Hopia appressed branches and oval spikelets versus Cynodon digitately arranged thin one-sided fingers.

four_real_central_texas_photos_20261022.arrow_audit_note: Visually inspected the actual four GitHub binary JPEG originals. Flower images: a full smooth oval spikelet and feathery purple stigmas. PAOB-C: attached leaf sheaths and slender culm only, NOT rooting node. PAOB-L: blade/sheath boundary and lower culm only, NOT measured free ligule margin. No fake caryopsis/glume-specific arrows.

measured_reproductive_key_20261023.look_here_first: Trace a surface runner to a hairy swollen node; then inspect a narrow flowering head with 1–4 short appressed racemes and blunt 3.4–4 mm spikelets. Confirm true membranous ligule and mature glumes, not head silhouette alone.
measured_diagnostic_key: GROWTH: warm-season creeping perennial with stolons/shallow rhizomes; a hairy node alone does not prove visible adventitious roots.
HEAD: Kew GrassBase 1–4 appressed racemes 1–2 cm long, central axis 3–10(–14) cm; historical Intermountain account 2–6 branches. Do not use branch count as rigid boundary.
SPIKELETS: Kew 3.4–4 mm, oblong to obovate, blunt, two florets: lower staminate and upper fertile. Intermountain treatment 2.8–4.4 mm; measured ranges vary.
LOWER GLUME: Kew 0.9–1 times spikelet length, 5 veins; older Intermountain account about 0.75 length and 5–7 veins. Preserve source disagreement.
UPPER GLUME: Kew about spikelet length, 7 veins. LOWER STAMINATE LEMMA: about spikelet length, 7 veins, with palea. Never call lower lemma an upper glume.
UPPER FERTILE LEMMA: Kew 3.4–4 mm, hard/shiny, finely reticulate, margins inrolled, blunt; no long protruding lemma awn.
LIGULE: true 1–2 mm eciliate MEMBRANE at inner blade/sheath junction; hairy runner nodes and sheath hairs are not the ligule.
measured_reproductive_key_20261023.local_lookalikes: Cynodon dactylon: several digitate slender racemes, smaller narrow spikelets and short hair-fringed ligule despite similar runners. Panicum virgatum: tall upright growth and open panicle, not Hopia's short appressed racemes plus hairy runners. Bouteloua dactyloides: low dioecious sod with different male/female flowering structures.

crew_confidence_gate_20261024.look_here_first: Trace a single long aboveground stolon to a swollen hairy node, then to an attached upright narrow head. On that SAME plant, look for 1–4 short appressed racemes and smooth, blunt, oblong-to-obovate mature spikelets around 3.4–4 mm. A hairy node without visible roots is not proof of rooting.

three_evidence_levels.requires: Vine-like runner or narrow blunt-spikelet head seen alone; photographs may show neighboring grass or detached stem.
three_evidence_levels.action: Record Hopia/Panicum obtusum candidate, photograph whole connection, do not infer species-level anatomy or rooting.

three_evidence_levels.requires: Same individual shows a runner with hairy swollen nodes plus upright head of short appressed racemes and several blunt, awnless-looking oval spikelets. Rule out Cynodon digitate fingers and Panicum virgatum's large open panicle.
three_evidence_levels.action: Teach the combined recognition pattern; if rootlets, true ligule, or mature spikelet scale are not actually visible, explicitly leave them unverified.

three_evidence_levels.requires: On source-vouchered mature material, measure five spikelets (~3.4–4 mm Kew), true inner eciliate membrane ligule (~1–2 mm), both glumes (Kew lower 5-veined, 0.9–1 spikelet length; upper 7-veined), lower staminate floret with palea, and hard reticulate awnless upper fertile lemma.
three_evidence_levels.action: Only annotate those organs after 10–20× pixel inspection and 1-mm scale. Source conflict: historical lower-glume proportion about 3/4, and historical 2–6 branches versus Kew 1–4; do not reject borderline specimens from one range.

exact_photo_order: NEEDS_PUBLIC_PHOTO 1 — Connected locally determined live specimen: centimeter-scale wide view from leafy shoot along ONE surface stolon to a swollen hairy node with actual emerging adventitious roots and onward to a flowering culm; photograph underside separately. Do not arrow roots on the existing PAOB-C culm photo.

NEEDS_PUBLIC_PHOTO 2 — Same plant, blade folded back to expose the TRUE 1–2 mm eciliate membrane ligule at inner sheath mouth, alongside a 1-mm ruler; mark membrane rather than nearby node/sheath hairs. Existing PAOB-L shows the collar region but does not establish free margin measurement.

NEEDS_PUBLIC_PHOTO 3 — Five ripe 3.4–4 mm oval spikelets photographed face-on and side-on with 1-mm scale; one dissected specimen separately exposes both glumes, lower staminate lemma/palea and hard shiny reticulate fertile lemma. Show where awn is absent, not a fictitious awn insertion.

NEEDS_PUBLIC_PHOTO 4 — Same-angle, same-scale Hopia versus introduced Cynodon dactylon: attached short appressed racemes/large blunt spikelets versus digitate slender fingers/smaller units, with connected runners when available.

field_photo_quickcheck.heading: Vine mesquite — runners, real panicle and collar
steps: START with the source-identified Central Texas flowering panicle (Bob Harms photo i, panel 5); follow attached branches and blunt spikelets.
CHECK the flowering-unit macro (Harms j, panel 6). Broad arrows do not certify individual glumes, fertile lemmas, or stigma dimensions.
OPEN THE COLLAR via archived stem/sheath and blade–sheath photographs (Harms c and l, panels 7–8). They show the junction, not a calibrated ligule measurement.
FIELD PHOTO HOLD: image a connected ABOVEGROUND runner with two rooted nodes and live leaves beside a centimeter ruler; existing images do not prove it.
COMPARE creeping-grass look-alikes with same-stage roots and real flowering structures; sprawling posture alone is insufficient.
field_photo_quickcheck.field_rule: Connected rooted runner plus diagnostic slender flowering branches with blunt spikelets; confirm collar from same plant.
field_photo_quickcheck.warning: Six locally archived images and three remote-only source entries. Harms images copyrighted with credited educational permission, not CC. No attached rooted-stolon photograph or calibrated dissected mature spikelet. All eight teaching panels are Hopia, not a photographed side-by-side with Cynodon; panel numbers in this walkthrough are one-based, while field-ID photo_panel_indices are zero-based.

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 01 · LOOK HERE FIRST
field_id_short_tiles.short: Follow a vine-like stolon to a swollen hairy node; then inspect a narrow blunt-spikelet head
field_id_short_tiles.details: Vine mesquite is a warm-season creeping perennial. Trace ONE continuous aboveground runner to a swollen pubescent node and onward to a leafy flowering shoot; do not infer actual adventitious roots from a merely hairy culm joint. On that same plant seek short appressed flowering branches with smooth oval spikelets. Existing panels show the head and stem but not a proven rooted node.
field_id_short_tiles.status: FIELD-READY GROSS CUE; NEEDS SAME-PLANT ROOTED NODE

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 02 · CHECK THE TRUE COLLAR
field_id_short_tiles.short: Inner ligule ~1–2 mm: eciliate membrane, not the runner-node hairs
field_id_short_tiles.details: Unfold the blade from its sheath and photograph the free inner membrane at 10–20× beside a 1-mm ruler. Published descriptions give an approximately 1–2 mm eciliate membranous ligule. The eighth teaching panel (zero-based index 7, Bob Harms PAOB-L) shows the collar region, but not a calibrated free membrane; nearby sheath or node hairs cannot be measured as the ligule.

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 03 · FOLLOW THE FLOWERING BRANCHES
field_id_short_tiles.short: Usually 1–4 short appressed racemes ~1–2 cm; published counts vary
field_id_short_tiles.details: Follow the flowering axis rather than judging a detached cluster. Kew reports 1–4 short appressed racemes (~1–2 cm) along a central axis ~3–10(–14) cm; a historical treatment reports 2–6 branches. Count attached branches and photograph the full axis; branch number alone is not a rigid exclusion test. The existing Central Texas flowering panels illustrate real heads, not exact measurements.

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 04 · MEASURE THE TWO GLUMES
field_id_short_tiles.short: Mature oval spikelet ~3.4–4 mm; lower glume ~5-veined, upper ~7-veined
field_id_short_tiles.details: Select five ripe oblong-to-obovate blunt spikelets at 10–20× with a 1-mm scale. Kew gives ~3.4–4 mm; other treatments give ~2.8–4.4 mm. Separate the lower glume (Kew ~0.9–1 spikelet length, 5 veins; older account ~3/4 length, 5–7 veins) from the upper glume (about spikelet length, 7 veins). Do not arrow venation on the current undissected head photos. The linked flowering-unit photograph (zero-based panel 5) shows real attached oval spikelets, NOT separated or measured glumes; no glume-vein arrows are justified.

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 05 · IDENTIFY BOTH FLORETS
field_id_short_tiles.short: Lower staminate floret; hard shiny reticulate upper fertile lemma, no long awn
field_id_short_tiles.details: Inside a mature two-flowered spikelet expose the lower staminate lemma with palea (published about spikelet-length and seven-veined), then the hard, finely reticulate, blunt upper fertile lemma (~3.4–4 mm in Kew). Distinguish a lemma from an upper glume before adding labels. A long projecting lemma awn is absent; no existing photograph resolves all parts for accurate arrows. The existing flower close-up is NOT a dissection of the staminate and fertile florets, so this anatomy step deliberately has no diagnostic photo link.
field_id_short_tiles.status: NEEDS_PUBLIC_PHOTO — SEPARATE STAMINATE AND FERTILE PARTS

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 06 · RULE OUT BERMUDAGRASS
field_id_short_tiles.short: Hopia's short appressed branches and blunt ovals ≠ Cynodon's radiating fingers
field_id_short_tiles.details: Bermudagrass (Cynodon dactylon) also runs aboveground, but commonly bears several slender digitately arranged one-sided branches from nearly one point, with a very short hair-fringed ligule. Switchgrass (Panicum virgatum) has a taller upright habit and large open panicle; buffalograss (Bouteloua dactyloides) is low and dioecious. Require connected runner, attached flowering head and mature spikelets before a confident vine mesquite ID. IMPORTANT: all eight current gallery panels are source-identified Hopia; none is an actual Cynodon, Panicum virgatum or Bouteloua dactyloides look-alike photograph. Leave comparison links empty until properly licensed different-species panels exist.
field_id_short_tiles.status: FIELD-READY WRITTEN COMPARISON; NEEDS_PUBLIC_PHOTO — TRUE LOOK-ALIKE PANELS

grass_species_finalization_20261025.scope: Six concise practical existing-canonical-species tiles; no new media, arrows, taxonomy, native-range, genus/family, website or Pages edits.
grass_species_finalization_20261025.source_measurements: Kew: racemes 1–4 of 1–2 cm, axis 3–10(–14) cm; mature spikelets 3.4–4 mm, lower glume ~0.9–1 spikelet length and 5 veins, upper glume about spikelet length and 7 veins; lower staminate floret, upper hard reticulate lemma ~3.4–4 mm, awn absent; ligule 1–2 mm eciliate membrane. Historical sources vary in branch count, lower-glume ratio and spikelet length. Literature values are NOT measurements from existing JPEGs.

10–20× true inner ~1–2 mm membranous ligule at opened blade/sheath collar with 1-mm ruler; PAOB-L is not a measured membrane proof.
Five ripe attached ~3.4–4 mm spikelets face and side, and one dissected showing separately measured 5-veined lower glume, 7-veined upper glume, lower staminate lemma/palea and hardened fertile lemma.
Same-scale Hopia and Cynodon runners and flowering heads, with rights-cleared verified species and actual visible structures.

grass_species_finalization_20261028.look_here_first: Trace one connected creeping aboveground stolon to a swollen hairy node and attached narrow head; short appressed racemes carry smooth blunt oval spikelets, not Cynodon digitate fingers. Rooting at a node remains unproven in existing images.
grass_species_finalization_20261028.published_measures_not_photo_verified: Kew 1–4 appressed racemes ~1–2 cm (older account 2–6); spikelets ~3.4–4 mm (other treatment 2.8–4.4); lower glume ~5-veined and upper ~7-veined with published lower-glume proportion disagreement; lower staminate lemma and upper hard shiny reticulate fertile lemma, no long awn; true inner eciliate membranous ligule ~1–2 mm.
